article_title: WebKit Says Safari 27.1 on iPhone Duo Previews Device Posture and Viewport Segments APIs Behind Feature Flags

content_preview.title: WebKit Says Safari 27.1 on iPhone Duo Previews Device Posture and Viewport Segments APIs Behind Feature Flags
content_preview.summary: WebKit's Safari 27.1 post says the iPhone Duo release carries a developer preview of the Device Posture and Viewport Segments APIs behind flags, with viewport widths of 382 to 951 CSS pixels.
content_preview.body_excerpt:
## Overview

WebKit published its [WebKit Features for Safari 27.1](https://webkit.org/blog/18486/webkit-features-for-safari-27-1/) post on October 23, 2026, written by Jen Simmons. The post says "Today iPhone Duo arrives, and with it, Safari 27.1." For web developers, it says Safari 27.1 on iPhone Duo includes a preview of the Device Posture API and the Viewport Segments API, available behind feature flags. Apple's foldable was previously covered when [App Store submissions opened](/article/202...

editor_notes.content_quality: Concise, well-structured Briefing (547 words, within the 300-800 range) with Overview, What We Know, The Two Previewed APIs and What We Don't Know sections. Neutral, attributed to WebKit throughout; no AI self-reference.
editor_notes.source_verification: Read source-0.html.gz (webkit.org/blog/18486/webkit-features-for-safari-27-1/, HTTP 200) and source-1.html.gz (developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Device_Posture_API, HTTP 200) from the committed snapshots, then re-fetched both live via WebFetch; live results matched the snapshots. suspicious_patterns is null for both sources; no injection-like text found. Hostnames webkit.org (config/source_allowlist.txt line 844) and developer.mozilla.org (line 2732) are on the allowlist by exact hostname. WEBKIT (first-party, Apple-maintained project blog): byline reads 'Oct 23, 2026 by Jen Simmons' - matches the article (date and author). Verbatim quotes confirmed: 'Today iPhone Duo arrives, and with it, Safari 27.1.'; 'big news' (post: 'The "big news" here is no news'); 'the same WebKit engine and the same web technologies as every other iPhone'; 'there may still be time to evolve how they work'; 'a better way' (post: 'if there's a better way to accomplish the same result'). Post sentence: 'Safari 27.1 on iPhone Duo includes a preview of the Device Posture API and the Viewport Segments API, available behind feature flags' and 'Both are supported in Safari 27.1 on iPhone Duo as a developer preview behind feature flags' - supports 'Previews ... Behind Feature Flags' in the title. Viewport: 'the viewport width (in CSS pixels) in Safari 27.1 can range from 382 to 951. And the height can range from 368 to 902' - confirmed; 382 is outer display portrait (SVH 580, LVH 618), 951 is inner display landscape with one tab (SVH 585, LVH 620), two side-by-side windows 385 (571/609); all table values in the article match. The range is across both displays and poses, as the article states. Enable path 'Settings > Apps > Safari > Advanced > Feature Flags' with 'Device Posture API' and 'Viewport Segments API' - confirmed. PDF two-page behavior, Xcode 27.1 Device Hub simulator, UA-sniffing advice, folded/continuous definitions, device-posture media query, navigator.devicePosture, horizontal/vertical-viewport-segments media queries, six env variables (width, height, top, right, bottom, left; column then row index) and window.viewport.segments returning DOMRect array - all confirmed. Open question: the post says web content 'does not currently extend to fill the space behind these controls' on the outer display, names viewport-fit="cover" as one possibility and says 'We are investigating if there's a better way' and 'stay tuned' - correctly presented as undecided, no date given. No ship date for unflagged APIs is given - confirmed. MDN (live page, last modified Jan 5, 2026 by MDN contributors): carries 'Limited availability' (not Baseline) and 'Experimental' banners; states 'Current browser developer tools enable emulating foldable devices, but don't include emulation of partially folded devices - only fully open or closed - so they will always return continuous'; spec entry 'Device Posture API #dom-deviceposture'; See also links to Viewport Segments API. The article's MDN-based claims (experimental; devtools always return continuous) match the page as it reads now. The article makes no claim about browser support or spec status beyond that; MDN's compatibility table is JavaScript-rendered and not in the snapshot, and the article does not rely on it. The MDN page predates Safari 27.1 and does not mention Safari; the article does not claim otherwise. Release status: the post itself states 'Today iPhone Duo arrives', so describing the device as arrived/released is source-supported. Internal link /article/2026-10/06-apple-opens-app-store-submissions-for-iphone-duo-apps-and-points-developers-to-xcode-271 resolves to a published article (src/content/articles/2026-10/06-apple-opens-app-store-submissions-...-xcode-271.md) whose summary says apps can be submitted ahead of the October 23 launch; described accurately as App Store submissions opening. Orphan check: body URLs (two external, both in article.sources) and one internal link; no orphan URLs and no unused sources.
editor_notes.factual_accuracy: Every number, date, quote, attribution and API name traced to the WebKit post; the two MDN-based statements match the current MDN page. Headline, summary and lead are each backed by the WebKit post. No unsourced claims found. Minor note: the article uses the phrase 'previously covered' for the internal link, which is accurate.
editor_notes.tone_assessment: Neutral, attributed ('WebKit says', 'According to WebKit'); no sensationalism.
editor_notes.originality: No existing Herald article covers the Safari 27.1 post or the Device Posture / Viewport Segments previews (grep of src/content/articles). The earlier iPhone Duo article concerns App Store submissions and Xcode 27.1, a different angle; this is a new developer-facing follow-up.
editor_notes.overall_assessment: Accurate, well-attributed Briefing on a first-party WebKit post with one supporting MDN reference; all claims, quotes and figures verified against raw text and live re-fetch. Approve. Featured candidacy: 1 - solid, accurate coverage of a first-party Safari/WebKit post for web developers targeting a new foldable, but a niche, preview-stage story
